root_cause.text: The NFSd NFSv4.0 replay cache stored encoded operation replies in a fixed 112-byte `rp_ibuf` sized only for typical OPEN responses, but `nfsd4_encode_operation()` copied LOCK-denial replies—including a variable-length conflicting lock owner—into it without checking the encoded length, causing an out-of-bounds heap write when the reply exceeded `NFSD4_REPLAY_ISIZE`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `if (len <= NFSD4_REPLAY_ISIZE)` before `read_bytes_from_xdr_buf()` and otherwise sets `rp_buflen = 0`, and the updated comment in `state.h` states that `REPLAY_ISIZE` is sized for OPEN responses while “Some responses can exceed this. A LOCK denial includes the conflicting lock owner, which can be up to 1024 bytes (NFS4_OPAQUE_LIMIT).”

intent_record.intent_summary: Limit NFS replay buffer capture to payloads that fit within NFSD4_REPLAY_ISIZE and skip oversized copies.
intent_record.what: In nfsd4_encode_operation(), the code that populates so->so_replay from the XDR buffer was changed from always copying the remaining bytes and setting rp_buflen to that length, to conditionally copying only when len <= NFSD4_REPLAY_ISIZE; in the else case, rp_buflen is set to 0 and no copy is performed.
intent_record.how: At runtime, small replay payloads are still preserved in so->so_replay.rp_buf, but larger ones are no longer copied into the replay buffer. This prevents storing oversized replay data in the inline replay state and avoids an unsafe or unsupported buffer fill for long responses.

intent_record.intent_summary: Clarify the REPLAY_ISIZE sizing rationale and document why larger replay responses are not cached.
intent_record.what: The comment above NFSD4_REPLAY_ISIZE was rewritten: the old single-paragraph explanation of how 112 bytes was estimated for an OPEN response was reformatted into a structured multi-line comment, and new text was added explaining that some responses can exceed this size, specifically noting LOCK denials with up to 1024-byte conflicting lock owner data, that oversized responses are not cached in rp_ibuf and only rp_status is saved, and that increasing the constant would enlarge every nfs4_stateowner.
intent_record.how: This change does not alter code execution or runtime logic; it only updates documentation to clarify the sizing rationale and the consequences of exceeding the replay buffer size, helping maintainers understand why the constant is left small and what tradeoffs exist if it is increased.

This completes the variable-length write into the replay buffer. If len exceeds the 112-byte rp_ibuf capacity, this statement causes the out-of-bounds heap write.
This stores the encoded reply length for replay handling without validating it against the fixed replay buffer size, enabling oversized replies to be cached and later copied unsafely.
